chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not send a Prophet except with truthful narrations, and repayment of the entrustments to the righteous as well as the immoral.
ai.seo_question: What are the essential characteristics of all Prophets according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores that truthfulness (sidq al-hadith) and fidelity in trusts (adā' al-amānah) are the universal hallmarks of all Prophets, extending their reliability to both the righteous and the wicked. In Shia scholarship, this establishes a foundational criterion for prophetic legitimacy, linking the moral integrity of the Messenger directly to the justice and completeness of his divine message.
